title: Structural Tilt Drift After Storms
dataSources: Mould risk (`mould:risk`), crack meters (`crackmeter:reading`), HVAC filter life (`hvacfilter:life`), structural tilt (`structural:tilt`).
app: Building-health sensors — indoor humidity / mould-risk monitors, crack and tilt meters, HVAC filter-life trackers, and damp sensors — streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and ESPHome.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=structural:tilt storm_window=true
| bin _time span=1w
| stats max(abs(tilt_deg)) as max_tilt, avg(abs(tilt_deg)) as avg_tilt by sensor _time
| sort - _time
description: Tracks whether tilt sensors show unusual movement during or just after storm-tagged windows.
value: Storms often reveal weaknesses that calm-weather averages hide, so isolating those windows is useful.
implementation: Tag structural tilt readings with a storm-window flag and summarize weekly peak tilt by sensor.
visualization: Weekly sensor chart of average and maximum tilt during storm windows.
grandmaExplanation: It logs whether storms seem to make certain parts of the building shift more than usual.
